q2_gaps: a bare mass NP carrying a restrictive participial modifier inside an of-phrase ('boiling mire-essence'): the NP rules say a bare mass stays a kind constant, but a kind constant cannot carry the modifier by Member (and Inheritance would over-claim that all mire-essence boils), and nothing states that such a modifier licenses minting a witness
notes: 'the smell of X' correctly fails the nominalization-object verb-paraphrase test (the smell does not smell the essence), so the opaque genitive Possession rather than (Of ...) is right; 'boiling' correctly stays a participial adjective, the inanimate transitive subject correctly stays Agent, and the bare-plural object of a dispositional clause correctly stays the bare kind filler 'wraith'.
